# Second-pass review — CDSFL @ `8879c34` (v3.2)

Tree confirmed clean at `8879c34`. Full suite run in this sandbox: **4 failed, 4496 passed, 11 skipped in 379s** — not the brief's "4493 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed". All four failures are proven environmental (§6), but one of them exposes a new harness gap of the same family as the worktree-HEAD bug that invalidated the last review.

## 1. The table, verified row by row

| claim | verdict | evidence |

First-pass repairs spot-checked: `lookup_alias_any` (`:1671`, consumed `:10732`), `NOT_PROBED_NO_FALSIFIER` (`:2876`), seam at the primitive (shim patches `R.dispatch_to_model`; the real one lives in `runner_core.py:1209` and is imported into the runner's namespace at `:180`, so rebinding covers all nine sites — verified no other module in the run path imports it separately). All 52 tests in the four repaired-guard files pass.

## 2. What will STILL be silent on the next simulated run

**N1 — the shim's error contract reintroduces the exact defect v3.2 fixed, inside the simulation.** This is the most consequential finding. The real `dispatch_to_model` **raises** on transport death (`runner_core.py:1271` TimeoutError, `:1277` RuntimeError, `:1284` re-raised payload). The shim **never raises** — it catches everything and returns `"__DISPATCH_FAILED__:..."` as text (`sim_dispatch_shim.py:129–133`). But `resolve_fn` detects transport death by *exception* (`reference_runner_v2.py:4533`); any normal return reaches line 4543 and appends to `_routing_attempts` — "a model was genuinely reached." So in simulation, a `claude -p` timeout is counted as a reached model: it burns the sub-critical one-attempt (`:4613`) and, if every rung times out, mints `irreducible_escalation=True` on a critical (`:4661`) → `unverified_critical_count` skips it → **the simulated run can converge because subprocesses timed out**. Two consequences: (a) the transport-dead guard you just hoisted **can never fire in simulation** — `_routing_attempts` always grows — so the sim cannot exercise the schema's most consequential repair end to end, which is the question this brief asks; (b) this is not hypothetical — the v3.1 run measured 35% timeouts at 300s, and 900s reduces but does not eliminate them. Note the sentinel-string convention is correct for the *findings* path (the runner itself produces it at `:6947` and checks it at `:7014/:7098/:6600`); it is wrong for the routing, verification, sweep, and preflight paths, which all rely on exceptions. Fix shape: the shim should raise (e.g. re-raise `TimeoutExpired`, raise `RuntimeError` on rc≠0-with-no-output) and let each runner path apply its own error handling — that is what "same seam, same contract" requires.

**N2 — the FATAL directive check verifies a file whose content reaches no one, and Fable-SIM will run on an empty system prompt.** `system_prompt_path` is referenced **zero** times in `reference_runner_v2.py` and `runner_core.py` (command above); it is consumed only by `experiment_11_orchestrator`'s own run flow, which this harness does not use. The panel's directive arrives exclusively via the composer (`composer.py:248/:585` loads `cdsfl_core_formal.md` itself). The harness passes `run_experiment(exp_cfg, "", cfg)` — `cdsfl_text=""`. So when Fable-SIM's composition raises `FileNotFoundError` (verified empirically: `Model config not found: .../bench/cdsfl_r...`), the loud fallback at `:6784` hands it `""` — one panellist of six briefed only by the round prompt and operational directive, while the verified-on-disk core directive sits unused in the same `main()`. One-line repair: pass `cdsfl_path.read_text()` as `run_experiment`'s second argument; the fallback then degrades to core-directive-only instead of nothing, and the FATAL check starts guarding something that is actually consumed.

**N3 — CC2v verification will still not fire, and the 7-round change won't change that.** Round indices are 0-based; `verification_min_round=6` means round 7 of 7. Real exp45 converged at round 3; the v3.1 sim converged at round 3. If v3.2 reproduces the reference outcome — the harness's stated purpose — the run ends 3 rounds before CC2v's threshold. Either outcome is informative (reaching round 6 would itself signal divergence from the reference), but the table row's "fixed" is wrong as a prediction: the thing that was silent will stay silent, and `verified` counts will recover anyway via the falsifier path, which was the actual cause (§1, last row).

**N4 — the strength ladder is silently replaced by panel order.** `DEFAULT_FALSIFIER_STRENGTH = ("Codex", "CC2", "ChatGPT", "Gemini", "DeepSeek")` (`routing.py:61`) and `rank_falsifier_writers` matches labels exactly (`:87–90`). With `-SIM` labels, `ranked=[]` and all six land in `extras` in panel order — first rung CC2-SIM, not Codex-SIM. Routing still runs (unknown labels are appended, not dropped), but the sim exercises the unknown-model fallback path, never the ranked ladder Bench Run 2 will run. Same vendor-keyed-branch class `base_model_label` was built for; this is an uncounted instance. (Also: "Fable" is absent from the strength order, so in a real Bench Run 2 panel Fable is an extras-rung — consistent with your declined-to-invent stance, but it should be a recorded choice, not an accident of a 5-tuple.)

**N5 — domain mismatch against the reference outcome.** The harness passes `domain="software"`; exp45 ran `domain="statistics"` (verified in `45_memory_statistics_live.json` and the report). The composer renders domain-specific directives, so the sim's panel is briefed differently from the run it will be compared to.

## 3. Is the transport-dead repair correct? Yes — in the real path.

Traced fully: the sub-critical filter (`:4577–4579`) `continue`s before line 4601, so sub-criticals reach the flag under exactly the pre-hoist conditions with the identical value — one-attempt semantics unchanged. `error_routed` is consulted only at `:4578`, inside the sub-critical branch, so setting it on criticals at `:4613` is inert — confirmed by grep over all consumers. The DUPLICATE carve-out at `:4614` is right: dedup needs no dispatch, so a duplicate verdict with zero attempts is legitimate. `result.resolved` requires a rung to have returned code, so a resolve with zero attempts is impossible — no false burn. Two residual caveats, both minor: (a) if `route()` ever raises between set and pop, `_error_route_pending: True` leaks into the checkpointed registry entry; (b) the AST test pins where the flag is *set* but not the consumption branch at 4611–4615 — a future edit there passes the pin. Neither outweighs the fix. The real-path repair stands; its simulation-path shadow is N1.

## 4. What we both missed

N1 and N2 above are the principal answers — neither appears in the brief, and N1 sits at the exact intersection both passes were staring at (the seam and the guard, separately correct, jointly broken). Additionally: the harness's `target = REPO / args.target` (line 69) silently accepts an absolute `--target` (pathlib lets the absolute path win) and would then feed `_build_discrimination_overlay` the very absolute path the last fix excluded — the default is safe, the flag is not.

## 5. Bench Run 2 readiness — fails at scale, cannot fail at exp45 scale

- **`decomposed_dispatch`** (known, agreed): additionally note it *cannot ever trigger* at 20KB payloads, so the sim structurally cannot cover it — the gap is not just unpatched, it is unexercisable at this target size.
- **`_verification_step` truncates silently at 80,000 chars** (`:7729`, `source_code[:80_000]`) with no truncation declaration to the model — unlike the sweep (60k, declared) and routing prompts (declared, `:4340` region). At 20.6KB it is unreachable; on a large external target CC2v verifies findings against a prefix while reporting a full verification.
- **Vendor-keyed `MODEL_SPECS`/params** (`runner_core.py:186, :1237`): SIM labels get `{}` → default params and `L=∞`. Inert at sim scale and moot for real vendor labels, but any Bench Run 2 panellist whose label drifts from the `MODEL_SPECS` key (Fable?) silently loses its context budget gate — the same class as N4.
- **The `-SIM` strength-ladder gap (N4)** means ladder-order behaviour at Bench Run 2 scale is unrehearsed by any simulation.

## 6. The suite disagreement — four failures, all environmental, one instructive

`python3 -m pytest bench/tests -q` → **4 failed, 4496 passed, 11 skipped**. Proven causes:

- `test_falsifier_cannot_read_the_key`: 17 rejections vs the pinned 2. Cause is sandbox path relocation, proven directly — exp44 C0001's archived falsifier hardcodes `_REPO = "/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering"`; `scan_falsifier_source(code)` rejects it here ("a path outside the declared target") and returns `[]` when called with `repo_root='/Users/georgejackson/...'`. Not a guard regression.
- `test_the_committed_ledger_matches_bench_logs` and both `test_operational_scripts` failures: gitignored-but-load-bearing files (e.g. `bench/logs/build_experiment_2026-08-22/RESPONSE_MODEL_INDEX.json`) are absent from the sandbox. **The harness now carries the uncommitted diff and untracked files — but `git status` never lists ignored files, so ignored artefacts the tests depend on still don't travel.** This is the direct successor to the worktree-HEAD bug: the carry is still incomplete, just one layer deeper. Failure rate 4/4500 executed (0.09%, Wilson CI [0.035%, 0.228%]) — small, but the *class* matters more than the count.

## SY compliance

Every quantitative claim cited in the applied work was re-derived with two independent tools: Fisher exact for 23/39 vs 0/19 — scipy `6.044e-06`, mpmath exact hypergeometric `6.044e-06` (brief's `6.0e-06` ✓); Wilson 7/20 — statsmodels `[0.181, 0.567]`, manual z-formula via numpy identical ✓; Wilson 7/53 — `[0.065, 0.248]` by both ✓. The 23/39 and 24/39 counts were re-counted from the exp45 report JSON, not taken from the brief.

---

**Bottom line.** Nine of ten table rows are true as stated; the tenth (7 rounds) is true but won't do what it claims. The v3.2 transport-dead repair is correct where real money flows. But the simulation cannot currently falsify it: the shim converts transport death into model responses, so the next simulated run will exercise the schema end to end *except* for the one repair that most needed exercising — and can itself converge on infrastructure failure, which is the founding sin this project exists to catch. Fix the shim's error contract (raise, don't return) and thread `cdsfl_path.read_text()` into `run_experiment` before the next run; both are small, and both change what the run can prove.

This sandbox is disposable, so the full findings above are the deliverable — nothing was saved to project resources from here. The harness gap in §6 (ignored files don't carry) and the two pre-run fixes (N1, N2) are what I'd action first.
